documents.title: Proposed Faculty Syllabus Statement Options Concerning Artificial Intelligence
tiers: B: allow limited use of AI
documents.summary: A Faculty Senate committee proposal recommending that every syllabus carry an AI statement. It gives a general misconduct paragraph plus three optional course statements (embrace, limited, prohibit) that instructors choose among or replace.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule: it says faculty should include 'some statement' and offers 'a choice of more specific policy options' (embrace, limited use, prohibit), so the decision is handed to instructors and the options act as tiers.

units.why: The document recommends that faculty put an AI statement in every syllabus: 'It is suggested that all faculty include in their syllabi some statement'. It is a recommendation, so modality is should, and it fits P09 (AI statement in syllabus).
units.anchor: It is suggested that all faculty include in their syllabi some statement
units.frag_start: It is suggested that all faculty
units.frag_end: use of AI in their classes

units.why: Faculty may write their own statements instead of the supplied options: 'faculty are also welcome to write their own statements'. The decision about the course AI rule rests with the instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: faculty are also welcome to write their own statements
units.frag_start: Suggested options are provided below

units.why: The document supplies a menu of three options (embrace, limited, prohibit) from which instructors pick: 'a choice of more specific policy options'. Named categories of AI use are P05; the choice per instructor is also P04, but the named levels are the distinctive content.
units.anchor: followed by a choice of more specific policy options
units.frag_start: It is followed by a choice
units.fit_note: Also lets each instructor choose; P05 chosen because the options are named categories (embrace / limited / prohibit).

units.why: A general statement is meant for all syllabi and says that inappropriate or unauthorized AI use 'may be academic misconduct'. It classifies misuse as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: may be academic misconduct and/or a violation of discipline-specific professional ethics
units.frag_start: The inappropriate or unauthorized use

units.why: Misuse 'will be handled according to TCU's Academic Conduct Policy', routing cases into the existing integrity process. This is the formal procedure for handling misuse (P81); P36 covers the classification, which the previous unit records.
units.anchor: will be handled according to TCU’s Academic Conduct Policy or other relevant policies
units.frag_start: Such misuse of AI or other

units.why: The statement lists possible sanctions: 'failing the course, program dismissal, suspension, or expulsion'. Specific penalties are stated in advance, P37 (stated as 'may', not fixed).
units.anchor: may result in sanctions, including failing the course, program dismissal, suspension, or expulsion
units.frag_start: and may result in sanctions

units.why: The misuse statement extends to 'other assignment-help tools', not only generative AI. It sets the scope of what the rule covers, which is closest to P61 (defining the policy's scope).
units.anchor: Such misuse of AI or other assignment-help tools
units.frag_start: Such misuse of AI or other
units.policy: Misuse of AI or other assignment-help tools is handled under TCU's Academic Conduct Policy.
units.fit_note: No definition of AI is given; this only widens scope to assignment-help tools.

units.why: Option A is the embrace option: 'may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation'. AI is allowed by default with citation, so P02.
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation
units.frag_start: Artificial intelligence may be used

units.why: Option A and B require citation of AI use: 'with appropriate citation. Examples of such citations can be found online, for example at APA'. Students must cite AI use, P24; the APA pointer is a format reference, not tool/prompt detail.
units.anchor: Examples of such citations can be found online, for example at APA
units.frag_start: Examples of such citations can be

units.why: Students 'are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI'. AI output may be wrong and must be verified, P31.
units.anchor: You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI
units.frag_start: You are responsible for fact-checking

units.why: 'The use of AI should not replace your critical thinking, judgment, and topic expertise.' The student must stay the primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: The use of AI should not replace your critical thinking, judgment, and topic expertise
units.frag_start: The use of AI should not

units.why: Option B allows AI for some assignment types and not others: 'may be used for [assignment types A, B & C] with appropriate citation, but not for [assignment types D, E & F]'. Use is decided assignment by assignment, P04; no AI-use categories are named beyond assignment type.

units.why: Option B: 'If you are in doubt ... it is your responsibility to discuss your situation with the instructor.' Students unsure should ask the instructor, P10.

units.why: Option C is the prohibit option: AI and unapproved tools 'MAY NOT be used for course assignments except as explicitly authorized by the instructor'. Banned by default unless authorized, P01.
units.anchor: MAY NOT be used for course assignments except as explicitly authorized by the instructor
units.frag_start: Artificial intelligence (AI) and other unapproved

units.why: Prohibited activity: 'Submitting all or any part of an assignment statement to an AI'. Students may not paste assignment specs into AI, P20.

units.frag_start: Submitting all or any part

units.why: Prohibited activity: 'Incorporating any part of an AI-generated response in an assignment'. Students may not have AI produce submitted work, P19.

units.why: Prohibited activity: 'Using AI to brainstorm, formulate arguments, or template ideas'. This bans a use P15 would permit; the nearest type is P19 (AI producing the work) but this is about ideas, so UNCOVERED is safer.

units.policy: Students may not use AI to brainstorm, formulate arguments, or template ideas for assignments.
units.uncovered_note: A ban on using AI for brainstorming and idea generation, the opposite of the brainstorming permission in P15.

units.why: Prohibited activity: 'Using AI to summarize or contextualize source materials'. A ban on AI as a reading or study aid, the opposite of P14/P12; no type covers prohibiting these uses.

units.policy: Students may not use AI to summarize or contextualize source materials.

units.why: Prohibited activity: 'Submitting your own work for this class to an AI ... for iteration or improvement.' Students may not use AI to improve their work, P21 (check/proofread graded work); also feeds their work to AI.

documents.unit: Mary Couts Burnett Library (quoting the Student Handbook)
documents.title: TCU AI Policy for Students (Academic Misconduct 10. Unauthorized Use of AI), quoted by the library
documents.summary: A library FAQ quoting the one sentence of the student Academic Conduct Policy that governs generative AI. It treats use without documented instructor or syllabus approval as misrepresenting others' work.
documents.stance_why: The quoted rule says 'Using generative AI without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus will be considered equivalent to representing someone else's work as one's own', so AI is banned unless approved: restrict.

units.why: The quoted TCU policy says generative AI use 'without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus' is misconduct. AI is banned unless approved or stated in the syllabus, a fallback when unapproved, P06; P01 does not fit as syllabi may permit.
units.anchor: Using generative AI without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus
units.frag_start: Using generative AI without documented approval

units.why: Such use 'will be considered equivalent to representing someone else's work as one's own', classifying it as misconduct (plagiarism-like), P36.
units.anchor: will be considered equivalent to representing someone else’s work as one’s own
units.frag_start: Using generative AI without documented approval

units.why: The entry places the rule in 'Section IV. Policy - A. Academic Misconduct - 10. Unauthorized Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)', i.e. the AI rule sits within the Academic Conduct Policy's misconduct list; this records the library's pointer to where the student policy sits, a statement of institutional framework.
units.anchor: Section IV. Policy - A. Academic Misconduct - 10. Unauthorized Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
units.frag_start: Section IV. Policy - A.
units.fit_note: Only locates the rule in the student policy structure; no principles or scope are stated.

notes: The TCU IT AI Policy and the full Academic Conduct Policy were inaccessible; doc u2 is a one-sentence secondary quote. Doc u1 is a committee proposal with unconfirmed adoption. Coded UNCOVERED: bans on AI for brainstorming and for summarizing sources (opposites of P15 and P14); candidate type for prohibited helper uses.
